1//! splitting layout (GPOS) subtables
2//!
3//! The implementations here are directly adapted from the code in hb-repacker,
4//! with a few minor differences:
5//!
6//! - we don't use a context/interface for the tables, instead using a generic
7//!   'split_subtables' method similar to 'actuate_subtable_split' and passing
8//!   it a method for each lookup type
9//! - harfbuzz splits off new subtables but retains the original subtable,
10//!   shrinking it to fit. We skip this step, and generate all new subtables.
11

31/// A common impl handling updating the lookup with the new subtables
32///
33/// This is roughly equivalent to `actuate_subtable_split` in hb-repacker:
34/// <https://github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz/blob/d5cb1a315380e9bd78ff377a586b78bc42abafa6/src/graph/split-helpers.hh#L34>
35fn split_subtables(
36    graph: &mut Graph,
37    lookup: ObjectId,
38    split_fn: fn(&mut Graph, ObjectId) -> Option<Vec<ObjectId>>,
39) {
40    let data = graph.objects.remove(&lookup).unwrap();
41    debug_assert!(
42        data.reparse::<rgpos::PositionLookup>().is_ok(),
43        "table splitting is only relevant for GPOS?"
44    );
45    log::debug!("trying to split subtables in '{}'", data.type_);
46
47    let mut new_subtables = HashMap::new();
48    for (i, subtable) in data.offsets.iter().enumerate() {
49        if let Some(split_subtables) = split_fn(graph, subtable.object) {
50            log::trace!("produced {} splits for subtable {i}", split_subtables.len());
51            new_subtables.insert(subtable.object, split_subtables);
52        }
53    }
54
55    if new_subtables.is_empty() {
56        // just put the old data back unchanged; nothing to see here
57        graph.objects.insert(lookup, data);
58        log::debug!("Splitting produced no new subtables");
59        return;
60    }
61
62    let n_new_subtables = new_subtables
63        .values()
64        // - 1 because each group of new subtables replaces an old subtable
65        .map(|ids| ids.len() - 1)
66        .sum::<usize>();
67    log::debug!("Splitting produced {n_new_subtables} new subtables");
68
69    let n_total_subtables: u16 = (data.offsets.len() + n_new_subtables).try_into().unwrap();
70    // we just want the lookup type/flag/etc, but we need a generic FontRead type
71    let generic_lookup: rlayout::Lookup<()> = data.reparse().unwrap();
72    let mut new_data = TableData::new(data.type_);
73    new_data.write(generic_lookup.lookup_type());
74    new_data.write(generic_lookup.lookup_flag());
75    new_data.write(n_total_subtables);
76    let old_mark_filter_set = generic_lookup.mark_filtering_set();
77    for sub in data.offsets {
78        match new_subtables.get(&sub.object) {
79            Some(new) => new.iter().for_each(|id| new_data.add_offset(*id, 2, 0)),
80            None => new_data.add_offset(sub.object, 2, 0),
81        }
82    }
83    if let Some(mark_filtering_set) = old_mark_filter_set {
84        new_data.write(mark_filtering_set);
85    }
86
87    graph.nodes.get_mut(&lookup).unwrap().size = new_data.bytes.len() as _;
88    graph.objects.insert(lookup, new_data);
89}

91fn split_coverage(coverage: &rlayout::CoverageTable, start: u16, end: u16) -> TableData {
92    assert!(start <= end);
93    let len = end - start;
94    let mut data = TableData::default();
95    match coverage {
96        rlayout::CoverageTable::Format1(table) => {
97            data.write(1u16);
98            data.write(len);
99            for gid in &table.glyph_array()[start as usize..end as usize] {
100                data.write(gid.get());
101            }
102        }
103        rlayout::CoverageTable::Format2(table) => {
104            // we will stay in format2, but it's possible it is no longer best?
105            let records = table
106                .range_records()
107                .iter()
108                .filter_map(|record| split_range_record(record, start, end - 1))
109                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
110            data.write(2u16);
111            data.write(records.len() as u16);
112            for record in records {
113                data.write(record.start_glyph_id);
114                data.write(record.end_glyph_id);
115                data.write(record.start_coverage_index);
116            }
117        }
118    }
119    data
120}

122// NOTE: range records use inclusive ranges, everything else here is exclusive
123fn split_range_record(
124    record: &rlayout::RangeRecord,
125    start: u16,
126    end: u16,
127) -> Option<wlayout::RangeRecord> {
128    // the range is a range of coverage indices, not of glyph ids!
129    let cov_start = record.start_coverage_index();
130    let len = record.end_glyph_id().to_u16() - record.start_glyph_id().to_u16();
131    let cov_range = cov_start..cov_start + len;
132
133    if cov_range.start > end || cov_range.end < start {
134        return None;
135    }
136
137    // okay, so we intersect. what is our start_coverage_index?
138
139    // the new start is the number of items in the subset range that occur
140    // before the first item in this record
141    let new_cov_start = cov_range.start.saturating_sub(start);
142
143    let start_glyph_delta = start.saturating_sub(cov_range.start);
144    // the start is the old start + the number of glyphs truncated from the record
145    let start_glyph = record.start_glyph_id().to_u16() + start_glyph_delta;
146    let range_len = cov_range.end.min(end) - cov_range.start.max(start);
147
148    let end_glyph = start_glyph + range_len;
149    Some(wlayout::RangeRecord::new(
150        GlyphId16::new(start_glyph),
151        GlyphId16::new(end_glyph),
152        new_cov_start,
153    ))
154}

156// a helper to convert a write-fonts table into graph-ready bytes.
157//
158// NOTE: the table must not contain any offsets. intended for coverage/classdef
159fn make_table_data(table: &dyn FontWrite) -> TableData {
160    let mut writer = TableWriter::default();
161    table.write_into(&mut writer);
162
163    let mut r = writer.into_data();
164    r.type_ = table.table_type();
165    r
166}

168#[cfg(test)]
169mod tests {
170    use std::ops::Range;
171
172    use super::*;
173
174    fn make_read_record(start_coverage_index: u16, glyphs: Range<u16>) -> rlayout::RangeRecord {
175        rlayout::RangeRecord {
176            start_glyph_id: GlyphId16::new(glyphs.start).into(),
177            end_glyph_id: GlyphId16::new(glyphs.end).into(),
178            start_coverage_index: start_coverage_index.into(),
179        }
180    }
181
182    #[test]
183    fn splitting_range_records() {
184        let record = make_read_record(10, 20..30);
185        // fully before: no result
186        assert!(split_range_record(&record, 0, 5).is_none());
187
188        // just first item:
189        let split = split_range_record(&record, 5, 10).unwrap();
190        assert_eq!(split.start_glyph_id.to_u16(), 20);
191        assert_eq!(split.end_glyph_id.to_u16(), 20);
192        assert_eq!(split.start_coverage_index, 5);
193
194        // overlapping at start
195        let split = split_range_record(&record, 8, 12).unwrap();
196        assert_eq!(split.start_glyph_id.to_u16(), 20);
197        assert_eq!(split.end_glyph_id.to_u16(), 22);
198        assert_eq!(split.start_coverage_index, 2);
199
200        // range is interior
201        let split = split_range_record(&record, 12, 15).unwrap();
202        assert_eq!(split.start_glyph_id.to_u16(), 22);
203        assert_eq!(split.end_glyph_id.to_u16(), 25);
204        assert_eq!(split.start_coverage_index, 0);
205
206        // overlapping at end
207        let split = split_range_record(&record, 18, 32).unwrap();
208        assert_eq!(split.start_glyph_id.to_u16(), 28);
209        assert_eq!(split.end_glyph_id.to_u16(), 30);
210        assert_eq!(split.start_coverage_index, 0);
211
212        // fully covered
213        let split = split_range_record(&record, 5, 32).unwrap();
214        assert_eq!(split.start_glyph_id.to_u16(), 20);
215        assert_eq!(split.end_glyph_id.to_u16(), 30);
216        assert_eq!(split.start_coverage_index, 5);
217
218        // identical
219        let split = split_range_record(&record, 10, 20).unwrap();
220        assert_eq!(split.start_glyph_id.to_u16(), 20);
221        assert_eq!(split.end_glyph_id.to_u16(), 30);
222        assert_eq!(split.start_coverage_index, 0);
223
224        // fully after
225        assert!(split_range_record(&record, 30, 35).is_none());
226    }
227
228    #[test]
229    fn simple_split_at_end() {
230        let record = make_read_record(0, 0..4);
231        let split = split_range_record(&record, 2, 6).unwrap();
232        assert_eq!(split.start_glyph_id.to_u16(), 2);
233        assert_eq!(split.end_glyph_id.to_u16(), 4);
234    }
235
236    #[test]
237    fn split_inclusive() {
238        let record = make_read_record(0, 0..100);
239        let head = split_range_record(&record, 0, 50).unwrap();
240        assert_eq!(head.start_glyph_id.to_u16(), 0);
241        assert_eq!(head.end_glyph_id.to_u16(), 50);
242        let tail = split_range_record(&record, 50, 100).unwrap();
243        assert_eq!(tail.start_glyph_id.to_u16(), 50);
244        assert_eq!(tail.end_glyph_id.to_u16(), 100);
245    }
246}
